title: H253 — Drift Regime Conditional Activation of Cross-Sectional Reversal/Value Signal
rationale: arXiv:2511.12490 documents a cross-sectional factor claiming OOS Sharpe > 13 by activating value and short-term reversal signals ONLY during individual stock 'drift regimes' — periods when a stock has >60% positive days in its trailing 63-day window. The insight: reversal and value signals are noisy in non-trending stocks but highly predictive during sustained directional drift. Our H181 (industry-adjusted reversal) and H241 (cross-sectional momentum) run unconditionally — applying this regime gate could sharply reduce false signals. The 13-Sharpe claim is extraordinary and likely overstates live-tradable edge (the paper tests on specific universes and periods), but even partial replication — OOS Sharpe > H181's current OOS or H241's baseline — would represent a meaningful improvement. Implementation plan: (1) compute trailing 63-day up-day fraction per stock daily; (2) define drift_regime = up_day_fraction > 0.60; (3) apply H181 industry-adjusted reversal signal only when stock is in drift regime; (4) compare OOS Sharpe vs unconditional H181. Confirm gate: OOS Sharpe > H181_oos_baseline + 0.2. Secondary check: does regime gate also improve H241 (cross-sectional momentum) OOS? If yes → H253 becomes a conditional wrapper applicable to multiple cross-sectional signals.
